part.twoMotifs.title: Two motifs in a row
part.twoMotifs.summary: A sacrifice works when it prepares a second blow; without it, it is just material given away.
ex.tm.67nDK: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.tm.67nDK.hint: Look for a sacrifice with check that brings the black king to a square where it gets checked again.
ex.tm.67nDK.solution: 16.Rxe7+! The rook captures the bishop with check and draws the king to e7. After 16...Kxe7, 17.Bg5+ gives check and uncovers the attack of the queen on d1 on the queen on d4.
ex.tm.0y0yV: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.tm.0y0yV.hint: Look for a sacrifice that draws the black queen onto the same diagonal as the king.
ex.tm.0y0yV.solution: 17.Rxe5! The rook captures the bishop and draws the queen to e5. After 17...Qxe5, 18.Bf4 pins the queen against the king on b8.
ex.tm.t2rZ1: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.tm.t2rZ1.hint: The black queen and king are on the e-file. Think about how to open it.
ex.tm.t2rZ1.solution: 18.Nxd5! The knight sacrifices itself on the pawn on d5, and the pawn on e6 recaptures and opens the e-file. 19.Re1 pins the queen on e7 against the king on e8.
ex.tm.sbjFq: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.tm.sbjFq.hint: The pawn on e3 is one square from e2, and the bishop on b6 eyes the white king. What stops the blow right now?
ex.tm.sbjFq.solution: 15...Qxd6! The queen captures the knight that was giving check, and the pawn on e5 recaptures. 16...e2+ gives a discovered check from the bishop on b6, and the pawn attacks the queen on d1 and the rook on f1.
ex.tm.0IOmf: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.tm.0IOmf.hint: Look for a sacrifice that brings the black queen to a square where it can be pinned.
ex.tm.0IOmf.solution: 18.Nxf7! The knight sacrifices itself on f7 and draws the queen. 19.Bg6 pins the queen against the king on e8. After 19...O-O, which takes the king out of the pin, 20.Bxf7+ captures the queen.
ex.tm.vNJht: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.tm.vNJht.hint: Look for a sacrifice with check that brings the black queen to a square your knight can reach.
ex.tm.vNJht.solution: 17.Rxe6+! The rook captures the pawn with check and draws the queen to e6. After 17...Qxe6, 18.Nxg7+ is a fork: check to the king and an attack on the queen. After 18...Kf7, 19.Nxe6 captures the queen.
ex.tm.kwLJm: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.tm.kwLJm.hint: Look for a capture that brings the white rook to a square your queen can attack with check.
ex.tm.kwLJm.solution: 17...Rxc1! The rook captures the bishop and draws the rook on a1 to c1. After 18.Rxc1, 18...Qg5+ is a double attack: check to the king and an attack on the rook on c1. After 19.Ng3, 19...Qxc1 captures the rook.
ex.tm.pziyc: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.tm.pziyc.hint: The pawn on e6 defends d5. Look for a way to remove it.
ex.tm.pziyc.solution: 17.Qxf5! The queen captures the knight that was giving check, and the pawn on e6 recaptures. Without the pawn on e6, d5 is undefended: 18.Nxd5+ is a fork, with check to the king and an attack on the queen on b6. After 18...Kd8, 19.Nxb6 captures the queen.
